subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a self-contained TypeScript module for a futuristic militarized 2077 pickup truck, with armor plating, neon accents, a turret, rocket pods, thrusters, and a spiked bumper, built using the SDK's builder, rng, paint, and glow utilities.

I'm sketching out the skeletal structure with chassis, wheel joints, steering, turret yaw/pitch, and hinged doors/tailgate, then roughing out dimensions and a wedge-shaped hull using lofted sections along the body.

Working out the hood and cab geometry with tapered frustum shapes...

Adding more vehicle details...

Still planning box rotations, glow decals, and side plane textures for emblems, orienting each panel so text reads correctly from outside the vehicle.

Now I'm picking which decal textures to actually use (settling on a military-style text plate) and thinking through paint schemes: panelled metal for the hull, a mottled grey-blue camo blend for the cab, and darker weathering mixed in toward the lower body.

Working out tire paint and finalizing the overall structure for the model code, aiming to keep it around 350 lines with a mirrored loop for left/right symmetry.

I'm also nailing down precise dimensions for the wheels, hubs, and body width so the wheels sit correctly outside the chassis, plus planning dark wheel arch boxes along the sides.

Now I'm figuring out fender flares positioned above the wheels and splitting the lower hull into a central section plus flank armor pieces to avoid overlapping the wheels, then sketching the cab shape as a simple box spanning the mid-body.

Placing the cab and windscreen heights, then laying out the truck bed with angled walls, and positioning the turret pedestal with yaw/pitch joints and twin barrels extending forward, copying the sampler's joint axis conventions.

Now I'm adding rocket pods on the bed sides, roof accessories like a light bar, antenna, sensor dome, and drone dish, plus tail thrusters with glowing bells and a thin underglow box. I'm setting up the tailgate hinge and door joints with simple flat panels, then double-checking that the tyres and hubs sit flush at ground level before finalizing the mesh and returning the root.

Adding rim neon torus elements...
